key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches perovskite solar-cell recipe shortlists for high-performing experimental neighbors, without establishing fabricated-device performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize promising combinations of absorber composition, device layers, and processing before costly fabrication.
method: Generate candidate recipes using reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support against 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates were 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for random sampling and 10% for the strongest baselines.
watch_item: Experimental performance, seed robustness, and matched-budget advantage remain unproven; composition-family support falls from 65.4% at similarity 0.80 to 11.7% at 0.90.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
